stories.headline: Assam: TAIPA protests for flood compensation, preservation of monuments
stories.title: Assam: TAIPA protests for flood compensation, preservation of monuments
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: NAZIRA: The Tai Ahom Yuba Parishad, Assam (TAIPA), staged a sit-in protest in front of the Nazira Co-District Commissioner’s office on Tuesday, demanding adequate compensation and rehabilitation for people affected by the devastating July 19 floods, along with preservation and beautification of historical monuments across Nazira co-district.

The protest was organised by the Nazira Sub-Divisional Committee of TAIPA, in association with the Tai Ahom Mahila Parishad, Assam, following a call by TAIPA central committee President Diganta Tamuli, who was also present at the programme.
At the conclusion of the protest, memoranda were submitted separately to the Assam Chief Minister and the Nazira Co-District Commissioner through the Co-District Commissioner’s office.
Among its major demands, TAIPA called for a CBI investigation into the July 19 flood, alleging that illegal stone and coal mining may have contributed to the disaster.

It also demanded immediate payment of adequate compensation to flood victims, rehabilitation of affected families, and a special package of at least Rs 5,000 crore from the Central and State governments for rehabilitation and infrastructure development in Sivasagar district.
The organisation also demanded an inquiry into alleged irregularities in the distribution of the Rs 15,000 one-time assistance and immediate payment to all eligible families who have been left out.

stories.headline: Chief Minister Vijay has claimed ownership over 50 cents of poromboke land in Kodaikanal, alleges election petitioner before Madras HC
stories.title: Chief Minister Vijay has claimed ownership over 50 cents of poromboke land in Kodaikanal, alleges election petitioner before Madras HC
stories.summary: He also says, the Neelangarai bungalow was not inherited but acquired through a settlement deed executed by his father S.A. Chandrasekhar in 2005
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay has claimed ownership over 50 cents of government poromboke land at Vilpatti village in Kodaikanal, falsely declared a property sold by him for ₹35 crore at Padi in Chennai as his property worth ₹7 crore and wrongly termed his Neelangarai bungalow as inherited property, an election petitioner has claimed before the Madras High Court.
However, Mr Vijay said the allegations against him were baseless and the petition must be dismissed.

In the petition pending before Justice V. Lakshminarayanan, S. Dinesh, a voter from Perambur constituency, insisted the election of the Chief Minister must be declared null and void for “wilful and deliberate” suppression, misrepresentation and false declarations with respect to many of the immovable properties referred to in his 2026 election affidavit.
According to the petitioner’s counsel V.R. Shanmuganathan, Mr. Vijay had claimed to have purchased the Vilpatti agricultural land for a consideration of ₹30,000 in 1997.
Mr Vijay had also said, the present market value of that property was around ₹20 lakh.
However, an examination of the village ‘A’ register revealed the property was actually a government poromboke land, the counsel claimed.
Similarly, the Chief Minister had declared to have purchased a non agricultural land measuring 33,955 square feet at Porur in Chennai for a consideration of ₹9.13 crore in 2010.
However, examination of registration department documents revealed that he had purchased only 20,773 square feet for ₹7.5 crore.
There was no explanation for excess declaration of the extent of the land as well as the sale amount, the petitioner alleged.

He went on to state that Mr. Vijay had declared to be owning a ₹7 crore worth 11,854 sq.ft commercial building at Padi in Chennai and claimed to have purchased it for a consideration of ₹1.95 crore in 2009 besides spending ₹3.9 crore on construction.
However, he had sold the commercial building with a constructed area of 23,460 sq.ft for a consideration of ₹35 crore on February 12, 2026, the petitioner claimed.

Further, the court was told he had not purchased the commercial property in 2009 as it had been declared in the election affidavit and instead received it in exchange for his Korattur property from Tamil Nadu Housing Board.

article_sentences: New Delhi: Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, and other INDIA bloc leaders were detained by police from the Akashvani Bhawan here on Tuesday, after over nine hours of staging a sit-in at the premises near the ECI's office.
However, they were released latter.

Earlier in the day, INDIA bloc MPs tried to push open the gates of the Akashvani Bhawan as they intensified their protest against the Election Commission of India (ECI), demanding Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.
Holding tricolours and banners reading 'Save democracy', the INDIA bloc MPs on Tuesday commenced their protest march from Parliament to the ECI headquarters.
The Opposition leaders raised slogans against the CEC, the BJP and the RSS as they marched towards the ECI headquarters.
In view of the protest, Delhi.
Police and other security forces had been placed on alert.
Barricades were also set up outside the ECI office.
Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi, along with several other INDIA bloc leaders, were also detained briefly during the day after being stopped from heading towards the ECI's office.
Gandhi was stopped by several layers of police barricades while attempting to proceed towards the ECI headquarters.
He subsequently climbed onto one of the barricades and waved a large national flag, drawing loud slogans of support from the INDIA bloc leaders and workers gathered at the spot.

Speaking to reporters from within the premises of the All India Radio (AIR) headquarters earlier on Tuesday, he said around 300 MPs from both Houses of Parliament were stopped from meeting the Election Commission.

stories.headline: US, Israel must abandon path of confrontation: Dr Farooq Abdullah
stories.title: US, Israel must abandon path of confrontation: Dr Farooq Abdullah
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 6: The Jammu and Kashmir National Conference President, Dr Farooq Abdullah, Tuesday expressed deep concern over the ongoing crisis in West Asia, saying that the conflict has engulfed not only the region but has also had repercussions across the world. He appealed to all peace-loving countries, particularly Arab and Muslim nations, to utilise all available diplomatic and political avenues to help bring the present crisis to an end. "International institutions, including the United Nations and the International Court of Justice, should also play an effective role in facilitating reconciliation, dialogue and negotiations between the parties so that the region can be saved from further destruction. At the same time, Israel must be held accountable for alleged war crimes and genocide in Palestine," he said. Dr Farooq, as per a party statement, said that the United States and Israel must abandon their war-driven approach and make the protection of civilians and their lives and property their foremost priority. “War can never provide a permanent solution to any problem, and the use of force only aggravates the humanitarian tragedy,” he said. He also expressed deep regret over missile attacks by Houthi rebels towards the Holy cities of Makkah and Madinah. He said targeting or threatening the sacred places with any form of attack was deeply regrettable and had hurt the sentiments of Muslims across the world. He urged the Houthi leadership to refrain completely from such actions.

stories.headline: RBI hikes repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5 pc; changes stance to 'calibrated tightening'
stories.title: RBI hikes repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5 pc; changes stance to 'calibrated tightening'
stories.summary: Mumbai, Oct 07: After nearly three-and-half years, the Reserve Bank of India on Wednesday raised key benchmark policy rate by 25 basis points to 5.5 per cent in a bid to tame rising inflation amid continuing West Asia crisis. With the rate hike, home loans, vehicle loans and corporate loans would become expensive and EMI for existing borrowers would also go up. A hike in the short-term lending rate (repo) by the RBI marks a reversal from its previous policy action. The last repo rate hike was in February 2023, when the RBI raised the rate by 0.25 per cent to 6.50 per cent. It kept the rate unchanged through 2023-24 before beginning its rate-cut cycle in 2025. Announcing the bi-monthly monetary policy, RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra said the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) unanimously decided to raise the policy repo rate by 25 basis points. Meanwhile, retail inflation rose to 4.82 per cent in August as compared to 4.45 per cent in the previous month. MPC changed its stance to 'calibrated tightening' from 'neutral' and also underscored that rate cut is unlikely in the near term given the current conditions. Besides, MPC must have taken into account the recent actions by central banks of developed nations especially the US Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank. Last month, the US Fed effected a 25 basis points rate hike to rein in inflation brought on by spiralling oil prices and other factors. Prior to the Fed, the European Central Bank too raised its key interest rate by 25 basis points.

article_sentences: The Reserve Bank of India is likely to raise its key policy rate by 25 basis points on Wednesday, with several economists expecting the first rate hike in nearly three-and-a-half years as inflationary pressures rise amid the continuing West Asia conflict.
RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra will announce the monetary policy decision at 10 am after the conclusion of the three-day meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee.
A 25-basis-point increase in the repo rate would mark a reversal in the central bank's policy stance after four rate cuts totalling 125 basis points in 2025, followed by a prolonged pause.
The last repo rate hike came in February 2023, when the RBI raised it by 25 basis points to 6.50 per cent.
The central bank kept the rate unchanged through 2023-24 before beginning its rate-cut cycle in 2025.
The policy repo rate currently stands at 5.25 per cent.
A majority of participants in a PTI poll expect a 25-basis-point hike and a hawkish tone from the RBI at Wednesday's review.
However, views are divided on whether the central bank will change its policy stance.
While most experts said a rate increase was imminent, some felt the RBI could hold off on a hike at this meeting.
The government has mandated the RBI to keep consumer price index-based retail inflation at 4 per cent, with a tolerance band of 2 per cent on either side.
Retail inflation rose to 4.82 per cent in August from 4.45 per cent in July.

stories.headline: Rupee falls 10 paise to 96.45 against US dollar ahead of RBI monetary policy decision
stories.title: Rupee falls 10 paise to 96.45 against US dollar ahead of RBI monetary policy decision
stories.summary: Mumbai, Oct 07: The rupee depreciated 10 paise to 96.45 against the US dollar in early trade on Wednesday ahead of the Reserve Bank of India's monetary policy decision. The rupee is under continuous pressure amid persistent outflows of foreign funds from domestic equities and strong US dollar holding near multi-month highs above 102 (DXY), forex traders said. Moreover, investors are keenly awaiting the RBI's monetary policy decision for further cues. At the interbank foreign exchange, the rupee opened at 96.37, then lost ground and fell to 96.45, down 10 paise from its previous close. On Tuesday, the rupee settled at 96.35 against the US dollar. "We have the RBI monetary policy meeting today, in which the RBI is expected to raise rates by 25 bps with an outside chance of a 50 bps raise. The RBI may also raise the CRR by 1 per cent to 4 per cent to absorb the excess liquidity. "We await the RBI stance on the falling rupee which has lost more than 2 per cent in the last 1 month with oil demand and FPI demand for the US dollar keeping the rupee lower," said Anil Kumar Bhansali, Head of Treasury and Executive Director, Finrex Treasury Advisors LLP, said. The Reserve Bank of India will announce its bi-monthly monetary policy decision at 1000 hrs on Wednesday, with several experts expecting a rate hike after nearly three-and-a-half years as inflation pressures rise due to the continuing West Asia conflict. The RBI last hiked the repo rate in February 2023, raising it by 0.25 per cent to 6.50 per cent. It kept the rate unchanged through 2023-24 before beginning its rate-cut cycle in 2025. The RBI's policy repo rate currently stands at 5.25 per cent. Meanwhile, the dollar index, which gauges the strength of the greenback against a basket of six currencies, was trading at 102.02, higher by 0.19 per cent. Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, was trading higher by 0.91 per cent at USD 101.50 per barrel in futures trade. On the domestic equity market front, Sensex fell 460 points to 72,599.05 in early trade, while the Nifty declined 164.80 points to 22,610.85. Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) offloaded equities worth Rs 2,961.30 crore on a net basis on Tuesday, according to exchange data.

stories.headline: Inox Green Completes ₹550 Cr Acquisition of WWIL’s 4.5 GW Wind O&M Business
stories.title: Inox Green Completes ₹550 Cr Acquisition of WWIL’s 4.5 GW Wind O&M Business
stories.summary: Inox Green Energy Solutions Limited (Inox Green), part of the INOXGFL Group, has completed the ₹550-crore payment to acquire Wind World India Limited’s (WWIL) wind O&M business. In a press release, Inox Green, a listed renewable energy operations and maintenance (O&M) service provider, said it made the payment under a Business Transfer Agreement (BTA) through its subsidiary Vibhav Energy Pvt Ltd (VEPL). Under the agreement, WWIL’s O&M business will be transferred to VEPL as a going concern. As per the terms of the BTA and the Resolution Plan approved by the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), Inox Green will hold a 75% stake in VEPL after the business transfer and implementation of the Resolution Plan is completed. This will enable Inox Green to consolidate the transferred business’s financials on a line-by-line basis. Supported by the broader INOXGFL Group ecosystem—including planned large annual capacity additions at Inox Clean Energy and external projects executed by parent company Inox Wind—Inox Green said it is firmly on track to exceed 20 GW of serviced capacity in the near future. WWIL’s 4.5 GW Portfolio WWIL’s 4.5 GW O&M portfolio includes a marquee client base comprising the Tata Group, ReNew, Greenko Group, Apraava Energy, and Hindustan Zinc. The assets are spread across key wind-rich states, including Karnataka, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, and Andhra Pradesh. The portfolio generated approximately ₹580 crore in revenue in FY26 and benefits from contracted annual price escalation of approximately 5%. Following the transaction, Inox Green’s O&M portfolio stands at approximately 13.3 GWp as of June 2026, inclusive of WWIL’s portfolio and a separate approximately 2 GW wind O&M acquisition currently held as an investment. Inox Green said it expects to leverage operational efficiencies, advanced technology platforms, and group synergies to substantially increase the acquired portfolio’s revenues and operating margins. Commenting on the acquisition, Devansh Jain, Executive Director, INOXGFL Group, said, “This transaction will be a defining step in our strategy to build India’s largest and most technologically advanced renewable energy services platform. Wind World’s quality asset base and deeply entrenched customer relationships complement Inox Green’s strengths and reinforce our long-term growth ambitions. “The transaction substantially enhances our multi-brand OEM O&M capabilities and strengthens our ability to deliver superior operational performance across a larger fleet of wind assets.” Jain added, “We are now focused on a seamless integration of Wind World India’s O&M business, leveraging our combined capabilities to drive greater value for customers, accelerate growth and further consolidate our leadership in the renewable energy services sector.” Akhil Jindal, Group CFO, INOXGFL Group, said, “We are extremely pleased to announce that this milestone transaction has been executed within our disciplined valuation framework. The business has several synergistic opportunities and the transaction multiple works out to approximately 2x EBITDA, based on expected earnings after the full realisation of synergies over the next year. “As we integrate the acquired business, our focus will be on driving operational efficiencies, improving margins and unlocking synergies to maximize value creation.”

stories.summary: Mumbai: Aggregate revenue and net profit of the Nifty 50 companies are expected to grow in double digits year-on-year for the September quarter led by select companies from the automobiles, banking and finance, metals and oil and gas sectors. Revenue and net profit are likely to grow by 19.9% and 22.3% respectively according to the ETIG estimates. Their performance will also benefit from the lower base of 9% and 8.4% growth in revenue and profit in the year-ago quarter."The broader earnings outlook remains healthy, supported by improving domestic demand, strong credit growth, government spending and a recovery in private capex," said Feroze Azeez, Joint CEO, Anand Rathi Wealth.134753222Gautam Duggad, MD and Head of Sales, Institutional Equities, Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL) expects Nifty earnings to grow by 27% and that of the companies covered by the broking firm to increase by 22%."Excluding oil marketing companies, aggregate earnings for the MOFSL Universe are expected to grow 24% year-on-year during the quarter," Duggad said.Read more: How a 9-year-old Warren Buffett learnt a lesson on compounding by rolling snowballs on the lawn of his Nebraska homeThe operating margin at the aggregate level is likely to contract by a tad 20 basis points to 21.9% from the year ago amid input cost inflation. Azzez expects margins to remain mixed as benefits of lower commodity costs are normalising while wage inflation and higher crude prices are creating some pressure on margins. Duggad believes that the risk-reward for Indian equities over a medium and long term has meaningfully improved given healthy earnings growth, resilient macroeconomic environment and cooling valuations. "With earnings growth increasingly concentrated in select themes, we expect market performance to remain firmly bottom-up, favouring growth-oriented businesses that are successfully scaling up and strengthening their competitive positioning," Duggad said. He expects 15-16% earnings growth over FY26-28 for the companies under his coverage.Azeez of Anand Rathi remains constructive for FY27 driven by strong healthy domestic demand and credit growth, government and private capital expenditure, and improving corporate earnings. "For FY27, Nifty 50 earnings per share (EPS) is expected to rise to ₹1,240 from ₹1,088 with 14% earnings growth," he said.Sector viewAutomobilesDemand across automobile segments remained resilient with sales volume growing in double digits year-on-year in the September quarter, barring lower tractor volume amid irregular monsoon. While revenue of majority of the auto makers is expected to rise in double digits, profits and profitability may remain muted due to higher input costs.BankingNet interest income is expected to grow in low double digits year-on-year while non-interest income may decline amid lower treasury income due to firm bond yields. The asset quality is likely to stay stable.Capital GoodsFresh orders from segments including power generation, transmission and distribution, data centres, and infrastructure kept the order book ringing during the quarter. While domestic execution gained pace amid scattered monsoon trend, geopolitical disturbance in the West Asian region may result in slower order ramp up. Higher raw material costs will weigh on profitability though the impact may soften due to pass-though of higher costs in some projects.CementCement demand is expected to grow in higher single digit in the September quarter, helped by sustained construction activities in an otherwise seasonally weak quarter due to monsoon. stories.headline: Chief Justice calls for technological sovereignty, justice for farmers
stories.title: Chief Justice calls for technological sovereignty, justice for farmers
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 6: Addressing a special session of the 60th Diamond Jubilee Convention of the Indian Society of Agricultural Engineers (ISAE) at Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology of Kashmir (SKUAST-K), Shalimar, the Chief Justice of the High Court of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati, called for ensuring that technological advancement in agriculture is accompanied by protection of farmers’ digital, economic and legal rights. The three-day Diamond Jubilee Convention, hosted by SKUAST-K, brought together nearly 700 agricultural engineers, scientists, technocrats and students from India and abroad. The convention focused on themes including ‘Women Leading Engineering Innovations in Smart Farming’ and ‘AI and Robotics for Gen-Z Farming’. “Today, every soldier—whether it be a farmer, a scientist, a teacher, a lawyer, or a judge—will have to be equipped with that kind of technology,” he said, drawing a parallel with the changing nature of modern warfare and the increasing use of drones and other advanced technologies. Earlier, the Chief Justice visited the exhibition stalls set up outside the auditorium and reviewed technologies related to drip irrigation, crop monitoring and drone-based agricultural applications. He stressed the need to make such technologies accessible and understandable to farmers so that they can effectively adopt them. Speaking during the session, Vice Chancellor, Prof Nazir A Ganai SKUAST-K, highlighted the need to accelerate technological interventions in agriculture to unlock the sector’s untapped potential. He said while the Green Revolution helped India overcome food shortages, the country now needs to focus on technology, skilled human resources and innovation to address emerging agricultural challenges. The Vice Chancellor also underlined concerns related to technological and data sovereignty in agriculture, particularly with the increasing use of drones, sensors and digital platforms. He stressed that farmers’ rights must extend beyond markets, land and water to the digital domain as well. The technical sessions featured addresses by Shri N.S. Rathore, Former Vice Chancellor, MPUAT, Udaipur, and Former Deputy Director General (Education), ICAR, on “AI-Driven Agricultural Technology, Smart Skills & Advanced Agricultural Techniques”, and Prof. V.P. Singh, Distinguished Professor, Texas A&M University, USA, on “Mathematical Modelling of the Water-Energy-Environment-Food Nexus.” The session also highlighted the research and innovation ecosystem of SKUAST-K. Over the past five years, the University has generated 148 Intellectual Property Rights (IPRs), including 62 product patents and five global patents, besides supporting 115 student startups and more than 130 commercialised products.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Acquits Govt Clerk Who Already Served Sentence In 16 Year Old Bribery Case
stories.title: Supreme Court Acquits Govt Clerk Who Already Served Sentence In 16 Year Old Bribery Case
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday (05 October) has set aside the conviction of a government employee under Sections 7 and 13 of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 (PC Act) who had already served his sentence, holding that the prosecution failed to prove demand and acceptance of illegal gratification.

A bench of Justice Ujjal Bhuyan and Justice Atul S Chandurkar held so while hearing an appeal filed by the government employee who had already served his sentence, and had pursued the appeal only to “get his name cleared.”
The appellant was an Assistant in the District Education Office and the complainant (PW 1) was appointed as an orderly in a Government High School but was not paid his salary.
It was alleged that the appellant demanded Rs 5,000 as bribe in 2010 for releasing the salary.
Thereafter, the complainant approached the Vigilance Bureau pursuant to which a trap was laid down leading to the arrest of the appellant and recovery of tainted money of Rs 5,000.

The Special Judge convicted the accused (appellant) under Sections 7 and 13(2) in 2021, sentencing him to rigorous imprisonment for four years and a fine of Rs 10,000 for each offence, with concurrent sentence.
Thereafter, he appealed before the Jharkhand High Court which dismissed his plea in 2022.
Aggrieved by the High Court's dismissal, the accused (appellant) approached the Supreme Court.
Before the Supreme Court, the appellant apprised the bench that he had undergone the sentence and paid the fine, but wished to pursue the matter to get his name cleared.
He argued that demand and acceptance of illegal gratification were not proved beyond reasonable doubt and that the prosecution relied entirely on the uncorroborated testimony of the complainant.
It was pointed out that the alleged transaction took place inside the appellant's residence, in the absence of the trap team and without any shadow or independent witness.

It was argued that the recovery of tainted money could not prove demand and acceptance, and that the phenolphthalein test (which confirmed that the money recovered was tainted) was conducted belatedly.

stories.headline: Cabinet celebrates Modi’s 25-year head of Govt run
stories.title: Cabinet celebrates Modi’s 25-year head of Govt run
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 6: The Union Cabinet on Tuesday passed a resolution congratulating Prime Minister NarendraModi on completing 25 years of continuous leadership as head of government. Far more than a customary tribute, it celebrated the extraordinary journey of PM Modi guided by principle of 'Nation First and Citizen First'. The resolution said that three overwhelming mandates in Gujarat and support in three successive LokSabha elections reflect the enduring trust that public have reposed in PM NarendraModi. The ten salient features of the resolution capture the unbroken thread connecting his leadership of Gujarat with his leadership of India. The resolution traces how PM Modi carried Gujarat’s successful initiatives to the national stage. SWAGAT, through which he personally heard citizens’ grievances, received the United Nations Public Service Award in 2010. It later inspired PRAGATI, bringing governments together to review stalled projects, resolve obstacles and accelerate completion. Jyotigram’s separate agricultural electricity feeders similarly became a national approach, extending Gujarat’s experience across India. The resolution said that PM Modi’s sensitivity towards poverty grew from watching his mother struggle with everyday hardships and encountering deprivation during his travels. The resolution connects these experiences with programmes delivering homes, water, banking and healthcare. Nearly 60 crore Jan Dhan accounts, over 4 crore homes and 25 crore people moving out of poverty show how personal understanding became public action, bringing families dignity. The resolution said that PM Modi’s determination to help people shape their futures runs through the resolution. Approximately 3.5 crore women became Lakhpati Didis, while the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam provided for women’s reservation. Startups, skills and education reform expanded youth opportunities. PM-KISAN transfers exceeded Rs 4 lakh crore, while PM-JANMAN brought focused support to particularly vulnerable tribal communities, extending development to those historically left behind. The resolution gives particular emphasis to PM Modi’s willingness to pursue reform despite political risks. GST, welfare delivery reforms and the replacement of colonial laws demonstrate his determination to address longstanding challenges. The resolution said that his appeals on cleanliness, digital payments and local products drew citizens into change. It said that reform emerged as a sustained commitment of his leadership, strengthened by conviction, public participation and national purpose. The resolution said that under PM Modi’s leadership, public capital expenditure rose from Rs 2 lakh crore to over Rs 12 lakh crore, alongside highway expansion and railway electrification. Electronics production increased from around Rs 2 lakh crore to more than Rs 13 lakh crore. Defence production and semiconductor manufacturing further reflect his determination to strengthen India’s ability to meet its needs. The resolution said that PM Modi’s faith in technology emerges through achievements spanning everyday services and scientific frontiers. Jan Dhan, Aadhaar and mobile connectivity improved welfare delivery, while UPI transformed payments. The resolution said that developing India’s own COVID vaccines and landing Chandrayaan-3 near the Moon’s south pole demonstrated PM Modi’s vision of a scientifically capable, self-reliant, Atmanirbhar Bharat. Private space participation and work in artificial intelligence, quantum technology and biotechnology carry forward the vision celebrated in the resolution: technology improving lives while expanding national possibilities. The resolution highlights PM Modi’s ability to give India direction through global upheaval. During COVID, he united the country, backed domestic vaccine development and enabled rapid vaccination. opening: New Delhi, Oct 6: The Union Cabinet on Tuesday passed a resolution congratulating Prime Minister NarendraModi on completing 25 years of continuous leadership as head of government.
Far more than a customary tribute, it celebrated the extraordinary journey of PM Modi guided by principle of 'Nation First and Citizen First'.
body: The resolution said that three overwhelming mandates in Gujarat and support in three successive LokSabha elections reflect the enduring trust that public have reposed in PM NarendraModi.
The ten salient features of the resolution capture the unbroken thread connecting his leadership of Gujarat with his leadership of India.
The resolution traces how PM Modi carried Gujarat’s successful initiatives to the national stage.
SWAGAT, through which he personally heard citizens’ grievances, received the United Nations Public Service Award in 2010.
It later inspired PRAGATI, bringing governments together to review stalled projects, resolve obstacles and accelerate completion.
Jyotigram’s separate agricultural electricity feeders similarly became a national approach, extending Gujarat’s experience across India.
The resolution said that PM Modi’s sensitivity towards poverty grew from watching his mother struggle with everyday hardships and encountering deprivation during his travels.
The resolution connects these experiences with programmes delivering homes, water, banking and healthcare.
Nearly 60 crore Jan Dhan accounts, over 4 crore homes and 25 crore people moving out of poverty show how personal understanding became public action, bringing families dignity.
The resolution said that PM Modi’s determination to help people shape their futures runs through the resolution.
Approximately 3.5 crore women became Lakhpati Didis, while the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam provided for women’s reservation.
Startups, skills and education reform expanded youth opportunities.
PM-KISAN transfers exceeded Rs 4 lakh crore, while PM-JANMAN brought focused support to particularly vulnerable tribal communities, extending development to those historically left behind.
The resolution gives particular emphasis to PM Modi’s willingness to pursue reform despite political risks.
GST, welfare delivery reforms and the replacement of colonial laws demonstrate his determination to address longstanding challenges.
The resolution said that his appeals on cleanliness, digital payments and local products drew citizens into change.
It said that reform emerged as a sustained commitment of his leadership, strengthened by conviction, public participation and national purpose.
The resolution said that under PM Modi’s leadership, public capital expenditure rose from Rs 2 lakh crore to over Rs 12 lakh crore, alongside highway expansion and railway electrification.
Electronics production increased from around Rs 2 lakh crore to more than Rs 13 lakh crore.
Defence production and semiconductor manufacturing further reflect his determination to strengthen India’s ability to meet its needs.
The resolution said that PM Modi’s faith in technology emerges through achievements spanning everyday services and scientific frontiers.
Jan Dhan, Aadhaar and mobile connectivity improved welfare delivery, while UPI transformed payments.

The resolution said that developing India’s own COVID vaccines and landing Chandrayaan-3 near the Moon’s south pole demonstrated PM Modi’s vision of a scientifically capable, self-reliant, Atmanirbhar Bharat.

Private space participation and work in artificial intelligence, quantum technology and biotechnology carry forward the vision celebrated in the resolution: technology improving lives while expanding national possibilities.
The resolution highlights PM Modi’s ability to give India direction through global upheaval.
During COVID, he united the country, backed domestic vaccine development and enabled rapid vaccination.
During the West Asia crisis, timely decisions and energy security measures helped India withstand disruption.
The resolution said that his leadership combined immediate responses with capabilities built over years, giving the country resilience and confidence in difficult times.
It said that 2016 surgical strikes, 2019 Balakot air strikes, and 2025 Operation Sindoor illustrate the national security red lines established under PM Modi.
The resolution places these alongside the removal of Article 370, 'One Rank.
One Pension' and creation of the Chief of Defence Staff’s post.
It said action against Maoist terrorism and peace efforts in the Northeast bring out leadership combining national resolve with development, stability, and public trust.
The resolution links India’s rising stature with PM Modi’s ability to build cooperation across divisions.
Consensus at G20 and BRICS, advocacy for the Global South and the African Union’s G20 inclusion reflect his diplomatic leadership.
Vaccine Maitri demonstrated how India’s capabilities could serve others.
Honours from 36 countries underline the international regard accompanying PM Modi and India’s growing influence and contribution to shared solutions.
The resolution said PM Modi’s vision unites development, cultural confidence, and environmental responsibility.
Climate action progressed from Gujarat’s dedicated department to renewable energy expansion and international partnerships.
Yoga, millets, Kashi Vishwanath Dham, and Ram Lalla’s consecration strengthened India’s connection with its heritage.
The resolution culminated in renewed commitment to his vision of collective effort towards a prosperous, self-reliant, and developed India by 2047.
